title: Choose the visual world
question: Pick the visual language for three structural HTML prototypes. The prototypes will still disagree about the generation flow.

options.label: Darkroom Workbench
options.thesis: The prompt is the enlarger, the active batch is the developing tray, and the library is the contact sheet beside it.
options.viewport: A persistent workbench keeps the full setup above a broad contact sheet, with the active batch developing in place.
options.risk: A dark scene can feel heavy if the library loses enough breathing room.

raised.raise: The workbench owns the whole window as one coherent environment.
Job state changes alter the image area itself, not just a status label.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: photographer proof sheets and macOS Quick Look
options.thesis: The library is one calm sheet of images, with a precise generation strip always ready at its edge.
options.viewport: A large chronological image field leads, while the complete generation setup stays in a narrow fixed strip.
options.risk: This is the most familiar option and may feel less singular.

options.label: Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One generation moves through setup, queue, development, and result without hiding the whole sheet of choices.
options.viewport: The setup occupies one continuous horizontal sheet; submission folds it into an active batch while history remains below.
options.case: The state transition is exceptionally clear, but the paper metaphor is less native to image making.
options.risk: The fold idea becomes decoration if its state transition is not exact.

options.label: Working Grid
options.thesis: Every control, job, and image snaps to one visible working grid so the whole batch reads at a glance.
options.viewport: A compact top control band and large results grid share the same strict cells.
options.case: The hierarchy is strong and minimal, though the graphic voice may compete with personal images.
options.risk: Visible structure can become visual noise in a dense library.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.thesis: Providers and batches become directly keyed pages in a rigid broadcast index.
options.viewport: A numbered generation page sits above a keyed history index.
options.case: Direct addressing is fast, but the command grammar makes a personal visual library harder to scan.
options.kept: Every action gets a direct, unambiguous address.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Generation batches become plotted fields with provider and status encoded as marks.
options.viewport: The library fills the window as a navigable field around the current batch.
options.case: Browsing gains atmosphere but loses the obvious prompt-to-result path.
options.risk: The visual metaphor obscures routine controls.
options.kept: Image importance should read through scale before labels.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Prompts cut image blocks out of a live field and queue them for assembly.
options.viewport: A spatial work site shows references, prompts, and results as moving blocks.
options.case: The scene is memorable but does not identify with a small personal desktop utility.
options.risk: The concept adds interaction cost to every ordinary action.
options.kept: Commit the entire window to one environment rather than stacking generic cards.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A neutral sidebar, prompt modal, and rounded gallery cards executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Navigation sits left, history fills the center, and generation opens in a modal.
canonCard.risk: It repeats the structure that currently makes generation feel separate and unclear.
